The character

Mara Vance

Invented, not a real likeness. One Flux portrait was generated from a written spec and frozen as the identity anchor; every scene and the whole training set reference it.

Age / read34, early-to-mid thirties
BuildGreek heritage, warm olive skin, lean athletic, 5 ft 7
Faceoval, defined jaw, deep-set hazel eyes, thick dark brows, faint nose freckles
Distinguishing marksmall vertical scar through the right eyebrow
Hairdark brown, wavy, shoulder length, low bun with loose strands
Signature itemsmall tarnished silver coin pendant on a leather cord — every scene
Triggermara_vance

The scar and the pendant are deliberate: small fixed details are what a viewer — and a reviewer — checks first when asking whether it’s really the same person.

The scenes

A field expedition, dawn to night

Same twelve prompts, same twelve seeds, generated training-free with SDXL + InstantID + IP-Adapter FaceID off the anchor. Two weight configs — switch between them.

The measurement

Consistency as a number

Every frame’s largest face is embedded with InsightFace ArcFace (buffalo_l), L2-normalised, so cosine similarity is a dot product. Two questions: how alike are the twelve to each other, and how close is each to the anchor.

Config v1 · 12 frames
metricvaluetarget

Targets are the pass line, not the result. Both configs clear all four.

The finding

Identity and control trade against each other — on a dial

v1 (InstantID 0.65, IP-Adapter 0.75) locks the face hard: 0.83–0.86 against the anchor on every scene, standard deviation 0.019. But at those weights the adapters own the composition. Every scene collapses toward a centred head-and-shoulders portrait, and the pose ControlNet can’t override it — “Ridge hike” and “Departure”, both written as full-body, come back as headshots.

v2 drops InstantID to 0.45 and releases it at 45% of the denoise, IP-Adapter to 0.55, pose ControlNet up to 0.85. Scene detail returns — the coffee mug, the soil sample, the radio at the ear, the rain and umbrella, the market stalls. Identity falls to 0.756 mean but stays well inside target. Framing still doesn’t change: InstantID’s face-keypoint ControlNet keeps centring the head regardless.

You spend identity lock to buy scene freedom. There’s headroom above the floor — but a hard full-body shot is where a trained LoRA wins outright.

The other pipeline

The trained-LoRA path

Built · not landed

Flux + character LoRA — diagnosed to root cause, needs different hardware

Built
ComfyUI graph (smoke-tested), 32-image captioned training set bootstrapped from the anchor, ai-toolkit config, isolated venv. Training ran — loss tracked normally, checkpoints every 250 steps.
Broke
Every checkpoint renders as noise, in ai-toolkit’s previewer and in ComfyUI’s Flux sampler, at every strength. Weights are finite but scale-blown — one tensor at max-abs ~166.
Cause
ai-toolkit trained against a quantised (fp8) Flux base with low-VRAM offload — the only way Flux LoRA training fits 24 GB. That path produces a LoRA that doesn’t transfer to a clean model.
Fix
Train on a 40–48 GB GPU against full bf16 Flux, no quantisation. The LoRA then loads into the same graph, unchanged. The pipeline is staged for it — the missing piece is the training run.

Production recommendation

Which method, for which character

Recurring hero cast
Trained LoRA. Few characters, generated constantly. Identity in the weights frees the sampler to follow pose and scene — exactly where reference-based methods fight you. Worth the per-character training, on hardware that skips quantisation.
Long tail / one-shot
IP-Adapter + InstantID. No training turnaround. Keep identity weights moderate with an early release, lean on ControlNet for pose. Accept the composition fight (the v2 config).
Both paths
One eval gate. Every batch scored against the hero; anything below threshold auto-flagged for regen. The same 40 lines of ArcFace math regardless of where the identity came from. That’s the pipeline, not the vibe.

How it’s built

The moving parts

Scripts drive the pod; the character, the training data, the scenes and the scores are all pipeline output. No manual image editing.

character_spec.mdthe fixed identity sheet every prompt reads from
scenes.yaml12 scenes — prompt, pose ref and fixed seed per scene
00_setup.shone-shot pod bring-up: ComfyUI, 10 custom nodes, ~48 GB models, every dependency fix baked in
01_build_dataset.pyhero portrait → 12-pose bank → 32 varied training shots → captions
02_train_lora.shFlux LoRA training via ai-toolkit, isolated venv
03_generate.pyrender every scene through either pipeline — same seed, shared prompt and pose
04_eval.pythe scoring — ArcFace metrics, heatmaps, threshold filter, A/B compare
*.api.jsonthe two ComfyUI graphs, patched by node title from config

Honest limitations

  • The trained-LoRA pipeline is diagnosed, not delivered — see above.
  • The 32 bootstrap shots skew to frontal face closeups; a real subject’s photos would be a stronger training set.
  • ArcFace scores the face, not hair, build or wardrobe — those are judged from the contact sheets.
  • One character, one age and ethnicity, 12 scenes. A demonstration, not a sweep of the space.
  • No temporal / video work in this pass; FaceDetailer + upscale refinement specced but not run.

Run on a rented RTX 4090. The host was badly contended and the stack needed real untangling — torch/torchaudio ABI, numpy 1↔2, Flux-quant VRAM — all captured as fixes, so a clean re-run is one command.
